form.2. SHORT COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.

form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

familiarity with advanced programming and basic software engineering concepts.

cos.statement: Configure an AI-assisted developer workflow using context engineering and tool integration, given a set of software requirements and an agent orchestration framework, with all public tests passing and no warnings from the configured static analyser.

cos.condition: given a set of software requirements and an agent orchestration framework
cos.degree: with all public tests passing and no warnings from the configured static analyser
cos.differentiation_note: Focuses on the developer's workflow configuration and tool interaction rather than backend model training as in CSE701.
cos.rationale: Enables students to set up the basic collaborative environment with AI agents, establishing the foundation for subsequent workflow engineering.

cos.statement: Decompose a natural language software specification into modular, executable specifications, using a spec-driven development tool, justifying each design decision against at least one stated requirement.
cos.behaviour: a natural language software specification into modular, executable specifications
cos.degree: justifying each design decision against at least one stated requirement
cos.differentiation_note: Focuses on translating requirements into agent-readable specifications rather than traditional manual requirements engineering in CSE582.
cos.rationale: Prepares students to feed precise intent into AI agents, which is critical for generating correct code in complex projects.

cos.statement: Implement automated test suites and evaluation loops for an agent-generated codebase, using a modern testing framework, such that at least 90% of the provided test cases pass.
cos.behaviour: automated test suites and evaluation loops for an agent-generated codebase
cos.degree: such that at least 90% of the provided test cases pass
cos.differentiation_note: Applies traditional testing concepts specifically to evaluate and constrain non-deterministic agent outputs.
cos.rationale: Ensures that students can verify and validate code produced by AI agents, maintaining software reliability.

cos.statement: Evaluate the reliability and efficiency of different AI-native development workflows, given a multi-agent software factory setup, identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence.
cos.behaviour: the reliability and efficiency of different AI-native development workflows
cos.condition: given a multi-agent software factory setup
cos.degree: identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence
cos.differentiation_note: Focuses on evaluating practical software engineering workflows rather than theoretical reasoning protocols in CSE594A.
cos.rationale: Allows students to critically analyze and optimize multi-agent collaborations, preparing them for real-world software factory roles.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. The curriculum addresses context engineering, the Model Context Protocol, specification-driven development, testing and evaluation loops for non-deterministic code, and multi-agent collaboration workflows. Students will learn to configure AI-assisted developer workflows, decompose software specifications into modular executable specifications, implement automated test suites for agent-generated codebases, and evaluate multi-agent software factory setups. The course is taught through lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions emphasizing hands-on development and experimentation.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules progress from foundational context engineering and tool integration to specification-driven development, testing loops for non-deterministic code, and finally multi-agent workflows. This sequence builds upon the mandatory prerequisite CSE201, ensuring students possess software development and testing fundamentals before tackling AI-assisted workflows.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix comprises assignments, a project, quizzes, midsem, and endsem examinations. This blend balances practical capability through hands-on projects and assignments with theoretical and analytical understanding evaluated via examinations and quizzes, aligning directly with the practical workflow orientation of the course outcomes.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE701 which focuses on backend AI models and algorithms for automated software engineering tasks, or CSE594A which emphasizes theoretical reasoning protocols for algorithmic problem solving, this course specifically targets the developer's interaction, workflow design, and practical collaboration with AI tools. CSE582 covers traditional software evolution and is distinct from this entirely AI-native course.
